One step of the stall counter

Source: R/imputeCellGLoc.R
dot-gloc_stall_update.Rd

The rule the stall counter of imputeCellGLoc follows, kept in one place so that it can be tested on its own. An iteration counts as progress when the weights' fixed-point residual dW improves by more than 1% on its own best so far or, under the categorical EM, when dR, the largest change of a categorical posterior, does. Progress resets the counter, anything else increments it.

.gloc_stall_update(dW, dR, dW_best, dR_best, stall)

Arguments

dW, dR

this iteration's weight and categorical-posterior residuals.

dW_best, dR_best

the best of each so far; Inf before the first iteration.

stall

the counter as it stands before this iteration.

Value

list(dW_best, dR_best, stall).

Details

Each residual keeps its own best rather than a joint one, so a fit whose weights have settled while its posteriors are still moving counts as converging and not as cycling. Keyed on dW alone it would count as a cycle, and the cold restart of .gloc_damp_schedule would then throw away every categorical iteration; on real survey data at a tight eps the posteriors are a plausible last-to-settle component. The relaxation schedule stays keyed on dW alone.

Without the EM, dR is 0 at every iteration: \(0 < 0.99 \cdot \infty\) holds at the first iteration and \(0 < 0.99 \cdot 0\) never after, so the counter follows exactly the pre-7.5.0 rule, which read dW alone.
